details.description: After the record-breaking global success of Spider-Man: No Way Home, Spider-Man: Brand New Day marks an entirely new chapter for Peter Parker and Spider-Man. Four years have passed since the events of No Way Home, and Peter is now an adult living entirely alone, having voluntarily erased himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime-fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he's devoted himself entirely to protecting his city â a full-time Spider-Man â but as the demands on him intensify, the pressure sparks a surprising physical evolution that threatens his existence, even as a strange new pattern of crimes gives rise to one of the most powerful threats he has ever faced.

details.name: Days Of Being Wild (4K Restored Version)
details.title: Days Of Being Wild (4K Restored Version)
details.description: Hong Kong, 1960. A sweltering hot summer. York (Leslie Cheung), an amoral disillusioned and cruel young man is kept in luxury by his foster mother, a retired courtesan, who gives him everything but the one thing he needs to know - the identity of his natural mother. A self-obsessed man, desperately seeking his true identity, York plays carelessly with his lovers, a lonely submissive bargirl (Maggie Cheung) and a beautiful club dancer (Carina Lau) and his friends, before leaving them all for the Philippines in search of the truth that has been denied, and may ultimately destroy him.

Night after night, the cityâs moral decay and grimy streets disturb him as deeply as the horrors of the battlefield. Adrift and disillusioned, he becomes fixated on saving Iris, a teenage runaway drawn into prostitution, setting off on a violent path of no return. Robert De Niro and Jodie Foster deliver landmark performances, embodying a chilling descent into self-destruction. Winner of the Palme dâOr and nominated for four Academy Awards, Scorseseâs raw portrait of urban alienation remains an essential diagnosis of a society defined by loneliness. Half a century later, the meter is still running.

details.name: Wakesurf Lovers
details.title: Wakesurf Lovers
details.description:
Amidst a rising wakesurfing craze, surf instructor Man (Renci Yeung) is falsely accused and publicly shamed online. Among the trolls is Chuan (Jeffrey Ngai), a surfing novice whose satirical video mocking her goes viral. Upon realizing the rumors were entirely fabricated and that he has ruined her reputation, a guilt-ridden Chuan signs up for Man's lessons under his real identity to make amends.


As they connect beyond the digital noise, a genuine romance blossoms. To clear her name, Chuan devises a plan to expose the disgruntled student who started the smear campaign, while encouraging Man to reclaim her professional standing by challenging celebrity coach Joe (Kevin Chu).

details.title: Swan Lake (Paris Opera Ballet 2026 - 2027)
details.description:
Broadway Cinemas is proud to exclusively present the Paris Opera Ballet's spectacular 2026-2027 season! Kicking this season off are two world-renowned ballet classics coming straight to the big screen: Romeo and Juliet and Swan Lake.

 

Prince Siegfried is urged by his parents to choose a bride, but by the shores of a lake he meets a mysterious swan maiden, Odette, enchanted by the sorcerer Rothbart. Only a sincere vow can save her. Captivated, he swears eternal love, until he meets Odile, the black swan...

 

A magical ballet set to Tchaikovsky's sparkling music, Swan Lake was first created in 1877 for the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow, later restaged by Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov. Nearly a century later, Rudolf Nureyev brought his own interpretation to the Paris Opera in 1984.

details.description:
In the seedy underbelly of 18th-century Paris, money is king. Nothing is sacred â even love itself can be bought for the right price. A native of this hedonistic underworld, Manon is caught between twin desires when she falls in love with the student Des Grieux. Steadfast and devoted, he offers the possibility of an honourable life. Yet, the riches promised by the world of Parisian society remain tempting...


Manonâs inner turmoil and struggle for survival lie at the devastating heart of Kenneth MacMillanâs 1974 adaptation of AbbÃ© PrÃ©vostâs novel. In this signature work of The Royal Ballet, MacMillanâs nuanced understanding of human psychology makes for an unflinching look into the moral degradation of Manonâs Paris, while all its decadence and decay are brought to life through Jules Massenetâs score and Nicholas Georgiadisâs designs.

details.description: Officer Yohji Ho meets a female android who comes from the future, in a drug raid. The android's mission is to ensure the death of Yohji, the elder brother of the future "Father of electronic Chips", so as to help the future scientist to become what he will be. At the meantime, Yohji is suspected as the murderer of a police officer. Scared and confused, Yohji flees and goes to Mei Ling, who looks identical to the android, for a fraud passport. Knowing Mei Ling is his brother's future wife, Yohji decides to kill her to save his own life. Being pursued by the police and the android, Yohji runs away with Mei Ling and starts their adventure.

details.description:
At a cosy Christmas party, young Clara meets the mysterious magician Drosselmeyer, who gives her a nutcracker doll. When the guests have departed and the house is asleep, Clara sneaks downstairs in search of the doll. Instead, she finds Drosselmeyer, who whisks her away on a journey into a whole world of enchantment: fantastical landscapes of flurried snow and glittering confection where toys come alive and the magic never stops. 


Peter Wrightâs production of this festive family favourite sparkles to the wondrous swell of Tchaikovskyâs orchestral score, alongside the glow and grandeur of Julia Trevelyan Omanâs period designs.

BAFTA Award-winner Lesley Manville (Phantom Thread) joins Aidan Turner (Rivals) in a striking new staging of Christopher Hamptonâs celebrated adaptation of the classic novel, where among the glittering salons of the super-rich, one misstep can mean ruin.
Marquise de Merteuil is a master in the art of survival. Alongside the magnetic Vicomte de Valmont, they turn seduction into strategy and weaponise desire. But when their alliance collapses into rivalry, the battle between them threatens to destroy everyone in their path.

 

Filmed live on stage at the National Theatre, Marianne Elliott (Angels in America) directs this thrilling game of love, lies, and social warfare.

details.title: All My Sons (NT Live 2026-27)
details.description:
Bryan Cranston (Breaking Bad) and Marianne Jean-Baptiste (Hard Truths) feature in a five-star, triumphantly acclaimed new production of Arthur Millerâs classic play, from visionary director Ivo Van Hove (A View from the Bridge).


One family, the heart of the American dream. When wartime delivers profits for Joe, it comes at a price when his partner is charged with criminal manufacturing deals, and his eldest son goes missing in action. Will peacetime bring peace of mind, or will he be confronted by the consequence of his actions?


Filmed live from the West End, Paapa Essiedu (I May Destroy You), Tom Glynn-Carney (House of the Dragon), and Hayley Squires (I, Daniel Blake) also feature in this disturbingly prescient play.

details.title: Queen Budapest (2026)
details.description:
On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the NÃ©pstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. 


Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracksâ"Bohemian Rhapsody,â "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Freeâ and "We Are The Champions." With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the countryâs top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity.

 

Donât miss Queen Budapest on IMAX screen and exclusive at Broadway Cinemas only !

details.name: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (KINO)
details.title: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (KINO)
details.description:
San Francisco, at the turn of the millennium. Monika Treut turns her camera on a community of artists, scholars, and performers who live beyond the boundaries of conventional gender, blending technology, biochemistry, and sheer boldness to reshape their identities on their own terms.

 

Asked whether they are male or female, the gendernauts simply answer: yes.

 

Made at a time when transgender lives were rarely portrayed with dignity or nuance, Gendernauts remains a landmark of queer cinema, celebrating gender not as a fixed destination but as an open, joyful frontier.

details.title: Oh, This Unspeakable Void (KINO)
details.description: At 20, Joachim is unexpectedly awarded a place at Munich's prestigious Otto Falckenberg School of the Performing Arts and moves into his grandparents' villa. Between the bizarre challenges of drama school and the eccentric, mostly alcohol-fuelled rituals of Inge and Hermann, he tries to find his place in the world. Simon Verhoeven adapts Joachim Meyerhoff's autobiographical bestseller with insane humour and deep feeling, directing his own mother, screen legend Senta Berger. A box office phenomenon with over a million admissions, the film won three German Film Awards 2026, including Best Feature Film in Bronze and acting honours for Berger and Michael Wittenborn.

details.title_lang: {"en":"The Einstein of Sex - The Life and Work of Dr. Magnus Hirschfeld (KINO)","zh_hk":"ç·æ¥µå (KINO)"}
details.description: Long before Kinsey, there was Magnus Hirschfeld: physician, sexologist, socialist, Jew, homosexual, and the man the tabloids dubbed "the Einstein of Sex." Rosa von Praunheim's affectionate biopic charts Hirschfeld's extraordinary crusade as he founded the world's first gay rights organisation in 1897, battled Paragraph 175, and opened Berlin's pioneering Institute for Sexual Science in 1920, a haven for queer and trans lives that flourished through the Weimar years until Nazi students torched its library in 1933. Friedel von Wangenheim plays the doctor with owlish warmth, flanked by his aristocratic great love Baron von Teschenberg, devoted young Karl Giese, and the institute's guardian angel, housekeeper Dorchen. Mixing period drama, newsreel and von Praunheim's trademark impish humour, it is both a monument to a man the Nazis nearly erased from history and a reminder of how quickly hard-won progress can burn.

details.title: Virgin Machine (KINO)
details.description: Dorothee MÃ¼ller, a naive young Hamburg journalist, has grown tired of her pushy lover Heinz. She shares an unfulfillable longing with her gay half-brother Bruno. In all innocence, she embarks on an investigation into romantic love â is it a disease that only afflicts women? From a pleasure-seeking hormone researcher's office to the chimpanzee enclosure at the zoo, her search yields no satisfying answers. So she leaves the old world behind, trading grey Hamburg for sunny San Francisco. Shot in striking black-and-white, Monika Treut's 1988 underground classic is a joyful, quietly radical journey into desire that remains as fresh and provocative as ever.

details.name: Good Bye, Lenin! (KINO)
details.title: Good Bye, Lenin! (KINO)
details.description: When Alex's mother, a devoted socialist activist, falls into a coma in October 1989, she misses the fall of the Berlin Wall entirely. Eight months later, she awakens, her heart too fragile for the truth. To keep her alive, Alex goes to extraordinary lengths to preserve the illusion of a world that no longer exists. A landmark of world cinema and one of the most cherished German films ever made, Good Bye, Lenin! endures as a timeless testament to love, memory, and identity. Tonight's screening is a heartfelt homage to its visionary director, the late Wolfgang Becker.

details.name: Ghosted (KINO)
details.title: Ghosted (KINO)
details.description:
An extraordinary love story between two worlds: Hamburg artist Sophie travels to Taiwan to come to terms with the sudden, unexplained death of her lover Ai-ling. In Taipei, a journalist latches onto her heels, seemingly obsessed with Ai-ling's fate. At the same time, the mysterious stranger does everything in her power to seduce Sophie.

 

Inspired by Taiwan's rapid social and technological development alongside ancient Chinese culture, Monika Treut weaves a narrative that drifts between past and present. At its core lie Chinese ghost myths, where traditionally oppressed women become erotic, daring beings who finally follow their own desires, and thus also find a way to take revenge.

details.title_lang: {"en":"It Is Not the Homosexual Who Is Perverse, But the Society in Which He Lives (KINO)","zh_hk":"éåä¹ç½ª (KINO)"}
details.description: Few films can claim to have started a revolution. Two years after West Germany decriminalised homosexuality, Rosa von Praunheim detonated this scabrous agit-prop fable on national television. Young, provincial Daniel arrives in Berlin and drifts through the gay subcultures of the era, from bourgeois coupledom to bar cliques to cruising grounds, while a merciless voice-over flays gay men for their assimilation, self-hatred and political apathy, demanding they come out and organise. The scandal was seismic: furious TV debates, walkouts, and the founding of dozens of activist groups. The modern German gay liberation movement traces its birth directly to this one film. Restored and as confrontational as ever, this is queer cinema as a molotov cocktail: crude, hectoring, frequently hilarious, and utterly foundational. Half a century on, its closing rallying cry âout of the toilets, into the streets!â still rings in the air.

details.name: Tough Love (KINO)
details.title: Tough Love (KINO)
details.description:
A karate champion looks back and finds his life reduced to bitterness and numbness. In childhood, he was repeatedly abused by his parents. As an adult, he became a pimp, earned large sums of money, and was eventually sent to prison. The only constant presence in his life has been his partnerâthe one person who supports him and gives him the courage to keep going. Caught in this vicious cycle, how will he confront himself, between who he was and who he is?

 

The film presents the life of Andreas Marquardt through an interweaving of interviews and dramatized reenactments, tracing a trajectory from fear and humiliation to contempt, hatred, and violence. Von Praunheim reconstructs the story through highly stylized scenes, capturing the interior design aesthetics of West Berlin at the time, and revealing the deep psychological trauma left by domestic abuse.

details.name: The Loneliest Man in Town (KINO)
details.title: The Loneliest Man in Town (KINO)
details.description:
Blues musician Al Cook lives surrounded by memories: his Viennese apartment crammed with vinyl records, videotapes, and a lifetime of devotion to a music he loves from an ocean away. When a ruthless real estate company targets his home for demolition, he must let go of his treasures one by one and face a radical new beginning.

 

From award-winning Austrian duo Tizza Covi and Rainer Frimmel, this quietly moving and unexpectedly funny portrait of loss and passion blurs the line between reality and fiction, bringing a real-life bluesman to the screen through non-professional performance and the warm, grainy textures of Super 16mm film. Premiered in competition at the Berlinale 2026.

 

Supported by Austrian Consulate General Hong Kong

Premiered at Cannes 2025 and received 6 nominations at the German Film Awards.

details.name: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Gendernauts: A Journey Through Shifting Identities (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: Before the world had the vocabulary, San Francisco had the âgendernautsâ. At the giddy height of the late-90s tech boom, Monika Treut embedded herself among the Bay Area's community of trans and gender-fluid artists, activists and academics: historian Susan Stryker, "Goddess of Cyberspace" Sandy Stone, video artists Texas Tomboy and Jordy Jones, intersex activist Hida Viloria, and the irrepressible Annie Sprinkle. These voyagers were charting identities beyond the binary decades ahead of the culture, and Treut films them not as case studies but as pioneers: partying, working, skydiving, remaking their bodies and their world with wit and ferocious self-possession. Winner of the Teddy Award at the Berlinale, this landmark documentary now doubles as a time capsule of a freer, pre-gentrification San Francisco, and as proof that the future arrives first at the margins.

details.name: Ghosted (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Ghosted (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: Grief has a way of following you across oceans. Hamburg artist Sophie Schmitt is undone by the sudden, unexplained death of her young Taiwanese lover, Ai-ling, and travels to Taipei with a video installation built in her memory. There she is pursued by Mei-li, a beguiling and persistent journalist who wants far more than an interview, and who soon materialises, unannounced, on Sophie's Hamburg doorstep. As seduction shades into investigation, past and present blur, and Monika Treut's cross-cultural mystery drifts elegantly toward the supernatural, steeped in Taiwanese ghost lore and the ache of unfinished love. The first German-Taiwanese co-production, shot between the night markets of Taipei and the grey light of Hamburg, GHOSTED premiered in the Berlinale's Panorama and remains one of Treut's most atmospheric works: a sapphic ghost story where the dead, like desire, refuse to stay buried.

details.title_lang: {"en":"It Is Not the Homosexual Who Is Perverse, But the Society in Which He Lives (HKLGFF 2026)","zh_hk":"éåä¹ç½ª (HKLGFF 2026)"}
details.description: Few films can claim to have started a revolution. Two years after West Germany decriminalised homosexuality, Rosa von Praunheim detonated this scabrous agit-prop fable on national television. Young, provincial Daniel arrives in Berlin and drifts through the gay subcultures of the era, from bourgeois coupledom to bar cliques to cruising grounds, while a merciless voice-over flays gay men for their assimilation, self-hatred and political apathy, demanding they come out and organise. The scandal was seismic: furious TV debates, walkouts, and the founding of dozens of activist groups. The modern German gay liberation movement traces its birth directly to this one film. Restored and as confrontational as ever, this is queer cinema as a molotov cocktail: crude, hectoring, frequently hilarious, and utterly foundational. Half a century on, its closing rallying cry (out of the toilets, into the streets!) still rings in the air.

Across two years of recurring rides, Hassan begins to recognise echoes of his own buried pain, and is finally pushed to confront the past that led him to leave his homeland thirty years ago. details.name: Two Mothers (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Two Mothers (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: At the age of 57, Rosa von Praunheim's 94-year-old mother told him a secret that rewrote his life: he was adopted. Only after the death of Gertrud, the woman who raised the enfant terrible of German cinema with unconditional love, did he dare to look for his biological mother, armed with little more than the name of a Riga children's home. What unfolds is a detective story through the darkest chapter of European history, leading through the archives of Nazi-occupied Latvia and the spectre of SS eugenics to a birth certificate discovered in a prison hospital, and to a biological mother whose fate proves devastating. Germany's great provocateur turns the camera unflinchingly on himself and finds his most tender register: part whodunit, part reckoning with the Second World War, and above all a love letter to the mother who chose him. TWO MOTHERS was a jury award nominee at Tribeca.

details.name: Virgin Machine (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Virgin Machine (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: Dorothee MÃ¼ller has a problem: she's a Hamburg journalist researching romantic love, and she can't find a shred of it. Ditching her dysfunctional relationships (and a hormone specialist's baffling theories), she flies to San Francisco in search of her runaway mother, and tumbles instead down the rabbit hole of the city's lesbian demi-monde, guided by strip-show barker Susie Sexpert (real-life sex guru Susie Bright) and magnetic drag king Ramona (Shelly Mars). Shot in luminous black-and-white by the great Elfi Mikesch, Monika Treut's sex-positive picaresque scandalised feminists and censors alike in 1988 and has since ripened into an underground classic: part German-expressionist satire, part sapphic travelogue, all liberation. Ina Blum is irresistible as the wide-eyed pilgrim who came looking for love and found her libido. The dildo lecture alone is worth a ticket.

details.name: The Secret Floor (KINO)
details.title: The Secret Floor (KINO)
details.description: When 12-year-old Karli moves to the Austrian Alps to help his parents restore a crumbling grand hotel, he stumbles upon a freight elevator with an extraordinary secret: it travels back to 1938. There he befriends Hannah, a young Jewish girl, and Georg, a hardworking shoeshine boy. When Georg is wrongly accused of theft, the three set out to find the real culprit and uncover something far more dangerous lurking behind the hotel's gleaming facade. details.name: The Einstein of Sex (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: The Einstein of Sex (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description: Long before Kinsey, there was Magnus Hirschfeld: physician, sexologist, socialist, Jew, homosexual, and the man the tabloids dubbed "the Einstein of Sex." Rosa von Praunheim's affectionate biopic charts Hirschfeld's extraordinary crusade as he founds the world's first gay rights organisation in 1897, battles Paragraph 175, and opens Berlin's pioneering Institute for Sexual Science in 1920, a haven for queer and trans lives that flourished through the Weimar years until Nazi students torched its library in 1933. Friedel von Wangenheim plays the doctor with owlish warmth, flanked by his aristocratic great love Baron von Teschenberg, devoted young Karl Giese, and the institute's guardian angel, housekeeper Dorchen. Mixing period drama, newsreel and von Praunheim's trademark impish humour, it is both a monument to a man the Nazis nearly erased from history and a reminder of how quickly hard-won progress can burn.

Hong Kong Premiere

 

In 1982, panic grips a remote Chilean mining town as rumors spread of a deadly illness said to pass between lovers through a single gaze. Eleven-year-old Lidia, raised by a vibrant queer cabaret family, watches them become scapegoats for the townâs fear. After losing her adoptive mother, Flamingo, Lidia begins searching for the truth. Blending harsh historical reality with lyrical magical realism, the film explores how fear is manufactured and how prejudice spreads. Winner of the Un Certain Regard Award at the Cannes Film Festival and representing Chile for the Oscars, this haunting and deeply moving film is a powerful testament to chosen family, resilience, and queer survival.

details.title: 25 Cats From Qatar (InDPanda)
details.description:
From the filmmaker of the award-winning CAT DADDIES (Opening Film of the 18th InDPanda). Qatar is one of the worldâs wealthiest nations, and its rapid growth is powered by migrant workers who make 89% of the population. But underneath the luxurious surface lies an overwhelming street cat population where disease is rampant, the heat is extreme, and expats are burdened to help the struggling felines.

 

When an American flight attendant and cat cafe owner becomes aware of the crisis, she hatches a plan to fly 25 cats to Milwaukee, where her cat cafe provides a pipeline for adoption.

 

This touching journey is both an urgent wake-up call and a compassionate and heartwarming portrayal of strangers overcoming international barriers to reach a common goal.

Adrift and disillusioned, he becomes fixated on saving Iris, a teenage runaway drawn into prostitution, setting off on a violent path of no return. Robert De Niro and Jodie Foster deliver landmark performances, embodying a chilling descent into self-destruction. Winner of the Palme dâOr and nominated for four Academy Awards, Scorseseâs raw portrait of urban alienation remains an essential diagnosis of a society defined by loneliness. Danger and desire bleed into one another in this neon-soaked descent into Sydney's queer underworld. Disgraced cop Aiden is reassigned to the city's gay nightlife district, where a charged encounter with Cody, a seductive bartender and sex worker, pulls him into the orbit of a murderous drag-queen mob boss and a deadly heist. As obsession curdles into self-loathing, Aiden's repression spirals gloriously out of control. Writer-director Dean Francis resurrects the erotic thriller and refracts it through an unapologetically queer lens, shooting the grimy glamour of Oxford Street's legendary Stonewall Hotel with style to spare. Tim Pocock, Tom Rodgers and a menacing Paul Capsis lead this baroque crime story charged with lust and betrayal. Premiering at Fantastic Fest, BODY BLOW is this yearâs campiest, sweatiest, and zaniest film yet.

details.description: May 1980, A taxi driver named Man-seob in Seoul, comes across an offer too good to be true. If he drives a foreign passenger from Seoul down to Gwangju and back, heâll be paid the unthinkable sum money â enough to cover several months of unpaid rent. Without stopping to ask the details, he picks up the German reporter Peter and sets off along the highway. There they encounter students and ordinary citizens taking part in large-scale demonstrations against the government. Man-seob, alarmed by the danger in the air, pleads with Peter to go quickly back to Seoul. But Peter ignores him, and begins shooting with his news camera. As time passes the situation grows more and more serious, and Man-seob keeps thinking of his young daughter at home all alone.

details.description:
Frameline Film Festival
Opening Film, Netherlands Film Festival

 

Asian Premiere

 

Amsterdam, 1986: the music is electric, The dance floor is heaving, and a generation of young gay men are living freely, defiantly, and gloriously as themselves. Ronnie spins records at the Downtown club, where he and the radiant Bas and restless Lennart forge a bond built on friendship, sex and euphoric excessâ¦ until regulars begin to vanish and the shadow of AIDS falls over everything. Thirty-two years later, reunited in the strange stillness of the COVID lockdown, the three survivors confront the choices and silences that shaped their lives. Director Michiel van Erp draws on his own memories of the era, weaving between two pandemics in a film that is at once a love letter to a lost generation and a portrait of how one carries on after surviving the unthinkable. Tender, euphoric and aching.

details.description:
New York City. JFK airport. A young woman jumps into the backseat of a yellow taxi, the cabbie throwing the vehicle into drive as the two head out into the night toward Manhattan... and strike up the most unexpected conversation.

Daddio celebrates the power found in those rare moments of pure human connection, even with the most unlikely person. This highly contained, yet kinetic character-study -- encapsulated in one single cab ride -- explores the complexities inherent to the secrets we keep, particularly the ones locked away on our phones. Itâs about truth and illusion, how we so effortlessly substitute one for the other out of survival. Itâs about the hurtful memories of childhood, how past trauma can manifest itself in the most profound ways. Itâs about the beautiful dance between the pain and poetry that is the human experience.

details.description:
Fantasia International Film Festival
New Zealand International Film Festival

Asian Premiere

The Faroe Islands, 1862: On a windswept rock in the North Atlantic, young fisherman Baldur lives a life of grinding routine until the mysterious and rugged Helge washes ashore, awakening something deep and dangerous within him. Beneath the crushing weight of family, faith and community, their mutual attraction must be kept secret at all costs. But when tragedy strikes, their forbidden passion unleashes forces darker than either could imagine, and the villagers rally to drive out the evil they sense in their midst. Adapting Karl Heinrich Ulrichs's 1884 novella, director Kasper Kalle pours new blood into vampire lore with a haunting, subversive queer folk-horror that recalls Dreyer and Robert Eggers. Egor Venned and Pilou AsbÃ¦k smoulder against the stark Faroese landscape. Premiering at Fantasia, this is gothic romance at its most full-blooded with a love that refuses to stay buried.

details.name: A Man Walks Down the Street (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: A Man Walks Down the Street (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description:
Best Narrative Film, Austin Film Festival
OUTshine LGBTQ+ Film Festival

 

Asian Premiere

 

Thirty years abroad have not loosened the knot in Raanan's chest. Now middle-aged and guarded, he returns to the Tel Aviv of his youth, carrying the weight of an unfinished life. But the hardest borders to cross are the ones he drew inside himself decades ago, long before he ever left. When a brief and electric affair with a much younger man ignites desire, confusion and shame all at once, Raanan is sent spiralling: caught between who he was, who he pretended to be, and who he might still become.

 

Writer-director Yuval Hadadi shoots his homeland with unflinching tenderness in a quietly devastating study of internalised homophobia and the long road to making peace with oneself. Named Best Narrative Feature at the 2025 Austin Film Festival, it is a portrait of a man finally daring to walk his own path.

details.name: Blue Film (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: Blue Film (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description:
Edinburgh International Film Festival
Athens International Film Festival

 

Hong Kong Premiere

 

In a rented Los Angeles house, two men strip away their personas in a relentless, unnerving battle of words. Aaron Eagle, a swaggering young findom camboy, accepts $50,000 to entertain a masked, camera-wielding client. But this stranger knows too much, and as the mask comes off, the night turns into a reckoning neither man may survive intact. What follows is a claustrophobic two-hander that refuses every easy handhold, forcing its audience to sit with shame, complicity and the discomfiting humanity of people we would rather look away from. Tony winner Reed Birney and the beguiling Kieron Moore (BOOTS) give fearless, vanity-free performances in writer-director Elliot Tuttle's incendiary 85-minute debut, lit in spectral Yves Klein blue. Passed over by Sundance and SXSW, BLUE FILM is a provocation on the morality of desire that no audience will leave quietly.

details.description:
Tribeca Festival

OutfestNEXT Los Angeles LGBTQ+ Film Festival

 

Hong Kong Premiere

 

It is Chinese-American actress Asherâs last night in Shanghai. After her last hip-hop dancing class, she asks her charismatic teacher, Tori, out for coffee. The casual date quickly heats up into a romantic night-time stroll through the city. Wandering under the night sky, they share quiet intimacy and a budding romance. This brief encounter brews into deeper feelings, making them wish the sunrise would never come. Inspired by BEFORE SUNRISE (1995), this tribute to classic romance cinema delicately captures the bittersweet tension of young female intimacy and their longing to be remembered. EPHEMERA is an irresistible, captivating watch.

details.description:
Morelia International Film Festival

After more than a decade living undocumented in the USA, Chuy is deported back to the small Sinaloa fishing village he once fled. But home has changed: drugs and the cartel now rule, violence is the texture of daily life, and Chano, his first love, has become a feared hitman. Thrown together again in this hostile landscape, their old romance reignites, forcing Chuy to choose between the man he never stopped loving and the future he longs to build. Writer-director Indra VillaseÃ±or Amador's debut feature sets forbidden tenderness against the brutal machinery of the narco world, a love story whispered through the streets of a place that has no room for it. Nominated for Best Mexican Film at the 2025 Morelia International Film Festival, GOODBYE LOVE is an aching elegy for love under impossible conditions.

details.description:
Best Ensemble Performance, Cinemalaya Independent Film Festival

Queer East Festival

 

Hong Kong Premiere

 

Hannah, Mihan, Charlie, and Kit, these four queer women in their 30s,  have dated one another at different points in their lives. Now living together as a chosen family, they consider their bonds to have evolved into deep, familial love, promising to face the challenges of early adulthood together. However, a bombshell dropped by Hannah uncovers everyoneâs unresolved relationship issues to resurface.

 

Remaining friends after a breakup, or being part of a large yet long-invisible bisexual community, this household reflects the diverse faces of todayâs queer women. Whether it is friendship, sisterhood, family, or romance, you are all on your own to decide if it is an ending or just a temporary pause.

details.title: Test (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description:
SXSW London
Jury Award for Outstanding First Narrative Feature, Frameline Film Festival

Asian Premiere

Small-town amateur bodybuilder Eddie keeps his eyes firmly fixed on the trophy. Living in codependent lockstep with his loving, alcoholic, evangelical mother (played by Emmy-award winner Tammy Blanchard), he waits tables, moonlights as a cam model, and channels every ounce of his turmoil into sculpting the perfect physique. But when a reputable new coach and a rekindled old flame enter his life, an unexpected flicker of queer desire cracks his carefully built exterior wide open. As his most important competition looms and his motherâs faith tightens its grip, Eddie must face his biggest hurdle yet: his true self. A standout of Provincetown and Frameline, where it shared the Jury Award with LEVITICUS, director Sam McConnell and writer-star Brock Yurich conduct a taut, tender myotomy of masculinity, faith and the soft, frightened self beneath the muscle.

details.name: What We Saw (HKLGFF 2026)
details.title: What We Saw (HKLGFF 2026)
details.description:
Hong Kong Premiere

 

In an era where daily life is inseparable from artificial intelligence, can what we see really be the whole truth?

 

At a school under constant A.I. surveillance, Mujin, a newly appointed teacher, is handsome yet somewhat naÃ¯ve. There, he meets Soyu, a brooding student who shares his passion for art. Mujin becomes deeply captivated by Soyuâs artistic talent, and a brief moment of physical contact between them unexpectedly sets in motion a complicated teacher-student relationship.

 

Told in two parts, Mujinâs memory and Soyuâs memory, the film reconstructs the same events through two radically different lenses. In the end, do we choose to believe the truth as determined by AI, or trust the instincts of human nature?

details.title: Bring Him Down to a Portable Size
details.description:
Writer Riko receives a call from the police that her older brother has died unexpectedly. As she travels to where his brother had been living, painful memories of their troubled relationship begin to resurface.

 

Riko reunites for the first time in seven years with her brother's ex-wife, Kanako, his daughter Marina, and son Ryoichi, who is now in temporary child welfare care. As they clean out the garbage-filled apartment where his brother once lived, old photographs and forgotten belongings reveal unexpected truths about the man they thought they knew. Over four emotional days, the four confront grief, resentment, and long-buried memories, ultimately rediscovering what it means to be a family.

When the PAW Patrol's archrival, Mayor Humdinger, begins recklessly mining in hopes of exploiting the island for its natural resources, he inadvertently causes a huge, dormant volcano to erupt. details.description: One sunny day, four young teens meet by chance at a crematorium. Hikari, Ikuko, Ishi and Takemura have all lost their parents at the same time. Hikariâs were in a car crash whilst on holiday. Ikukoâs were murdered by a deranged stalker. Ishiâs were in a gas explosion. Takemuraâs killed themselves to escape the hell of debt. But none of them could shed a tear. They were like zombies, devoid of all emotion. Alone in the world with no future, no dreams or even the energy to move forward, our protagonists dress themselves in scraps from a garbage dump, turn their favorite items from their empty homes into musical instruments, and decide to form a kick-ass band. They call themselves LITTLE ZOMBIES. This is a story about their quest to retrieve their ability to feel. And what they discover at the end of it.

While Fukiâs father is fighting terminal illness, her mother struggles with work and caregiving, estrangement develops between them accordingly. Fuki tries to figure out the complicated adult world and yearns for connection with the help of parapsychology. She places her fear and sorrow in miracles. details.name: Farewell to my Concubine (4K Restored Version)
details.title: Farewell to my Concubine (4K Restored Version)
details.description:
Douzi, a boy with feminine features, is abandoned by his prostitute mother to an all-boys Peking opera troupe supervised by Master Guan. Douzi befriends fellow trouper Shitou.

A few years later in 1938, a teenage Douzi is trained to play dan (female roles), while Shitou learns jing (painted face male roles). When practicing the play "Dreaming of the World Outside the Nunnery", Douzi intentionally mistakes the line "I am by nature a girl, not a boy" with "I am by nature a boy, not a girl," subjecting himself to severe physical punishments. Douzi along with another student, Laizi, attempt to run away, but Douzi decides to pursue acting seriously after witnessing an opera performance. Upon returning, they find the whole troupe being punished for their desertion, and Douzi is beaten. As a result, Laizi hangs himself...

details.description:
Heat is a gripping crime thriller directed by Michael Mann, starring Academy AwardÂ® winners Al Pacino and Robert De Niro. Neil McCauley (Robert De Niro), a highly skilled and disciplined professional thief who leads a crew specializing in high-stakes heists across Los Angeles. On the other side is Vincent Hanna (Al Pacino), a relentless LAPD detective whose dedication to his job matches McCauleyâs commitment to his criminal craft.

As McCauley and his crew plan their biggest score yet, Hanna and his team close in, leading to an intense game of cat and mouse. Both men struggle to balance their personal lives with their professional obsessions, blurring the lines between hunter and hunted. The film builds to a climactic confrontation, exploring themes of loyalty, sacrifice, and the thin line separating lawmen from lawbreakers.

Renowned for its realistic action sequences, complex characters, and the legendary face-off between Pacino and De Niro, Heat is considered a landmark in the crime genre.
